description: STRONG ADMISSION: one of the eight STRONG arms anywhere in title-or-abstract, with no positional and no citation requirement. This is the twelve-arm `replication-claim` this family replaces, minus its four residual arms — the broadest claim in the family and the one that carries most of its recall. The eight STRONG arms are the ones whose FLoRA yield and cached-screen precision survived measurement; the four RESIDUAL arms — `(fail*|unable|inabilit*|attempt*) to replicate`, `(aim*|set out) to replicate`, `success* replicat*` and the negation matrix — are held out in `replication-claim-residual` and are not carried here. Over the routed pool (release ec9497102a7e, 5,146,160 rows) the twelve arms admitted 89,113 rows to screen_expensive; only 8,898 of those were admitted on a title-position match, so the great majority of this tier's volume is abstract-position, exactly the rows the label pass did not read. One clause per arm, so each arm can be measured and retired on its own evidence — the engine attributes a hit to the rule, not the arm, so an arm's count is a separate evaluation of that arm's pattern. Every regex is carried verbatim from the twelve-arm `replication-claim` this family replaces. Note what is NOT in any arm. Bare `replications? of` is deliberately excluded: it is the highest-recall phrase in the book (40.4% of positives) and also fires on 82.2% of screen-confirmed negatives, and no cheap syntactic anchor repairs it — it is `replication-signal`'s last arm instead. `registered report of` is excluded because most Registered Reports are original studies. Reproduction vocabulary is out of scope entirely; it belongs to `reproduction-signal` and #155. Every tier of this family routes to the same pile, so precedence here decides ATTRIBUTION, not destination: which tier `filter_evidence` records for a row several tiers claim, and therefore the order a worklist can be worked in. The ordering is by measured specificity — cited-title (760), title (750), text (730), residual (710) — so a row is credited to the narrowest claim that reaches it. The whole family sits in the 700s strong-admission band for the reason the single rule did: it yields to the identifier/title/type discards above it (940–960), which say the record is not a paper at all, and it outranks `not-a-study-type` (500), whose claim is a fallible registry crosswalk — so a replication mistyped as `paratext` is screened rather than deleted. It sits below `replication-claim-title` (750), which is this same arm set restricted to title position, and above `replication-claim-residual` (710), which carries the four arms measurement did not support. A fifth tier, `replication-claim-cited` (740), once sat between this one and the title tier and asked for these same eight arms plus an author-year citation anywhere in the same text; it was removed on 2026-08-04 because over running text that citation is co-occurrence rather than a link, and the rows it claimed fall here — its arm list was byte-identical to this one's, so nothing it matched is lost. Its full match block and evidence are archived in rule_ideas.md. `vocabulary` stays null across the family: an admission to the two-voter screen is a request for attention, not a verdict about what the row is (CONVENTIONS.md, "Pile → filter_status"). OPEN SCOPE QUESTION: the per-arm evidence carried below was measured on the entry sheet and on 501 screen-confirmed negatives, corpora that the arms themselves helped assemble; the volume and FLoRA numbers in this family come from the pool and are not subject to that bias, but no per-arm precision here does.

measured.sample: 2,895 distinct replication studies with a usable abstract from `data/FLoRA entry sheet - replication list.csv` (3,851 rows, 2,978 distinct doi_r), text = ref_r + abstract_r as a proxy for the pool row's title + abstract; scored against 501 rows of `data/not_a_replication.csv`, papers that passed the old filter, reached the two-voter screen and were judged not_a_replication. Computed 2026-08-04, proposal SS1 (redesign/rulebook_v2.html).
measured.rationale: With all twelve arms this rule fires on 82.6% of the positives at 6.8% of the false-positive load (80.8% / 6.2% without the four marginal arms). READ BOTH DENOMINATORS AS WHAT THEY ARE. The recall figure is an UPPER BOUND: a substantial share of the entry sheet was discovered by keyword search, so a phrase rule scored against it over-estimates recall, most for the arms that did the finding; the sheet's columns do not separate curated-list entries from pipeline-found ones, so this is corrected by the SS6 holdout design, not here. The 6.8% is NOT a population false-positive rate and must never be quoted as this rule's precision: the negatives corpus is the false-positive load itself — what the old loose filter admitted and the screen then rejected — so what it measures exactly is the composition of the money currently being wasted. Per-arm firing on the 501 negatives: `we replicat*` 1.6%, `replicate and extend` 1.6%, `replication study` 0.8%, `fail/attempt to replicate` 0.8%, `study replicated` 0.0%, the qualifier family 2.8%. The four marginal arms were measured MARGINALLY, i.e. what each adds once the arms above it are in: `success* replicat*` +26 positives / +2 negatives (13:1, and the only arm carrying the successful-outcome framing); the negation matrix +18 / +1; `replication attempt(s)` +8 / +0; the failure nouns +1 / +0. That last +1 is the clearest case on the page of why a marginal count is not a coverage argument: 'We present a failed replication of Smith (2009)' fires the noun arm and NOTHING ELSE in this rule, because 'replication' there is a noun and the sentence never uses the verb. It scores +1 only because in this keyword-assembled corpus the papers phrasing it that way almost all also say 'replication study' or 'we replicated' somewhere in the same abstract. A marginal count of +1 on a biased corpus is weak evidence of redundancy; a marginal count of +0 negatives is strong evidence of harmlessness, and when an arm is free the second number decides. The rule discards nothing — it admits into a tier that decides — so the evidence gate does not bind it; this entry documents the claim rather than satisfying a gate.
